summary.title: Software Engineers Growth framework
summary.one_liner: ProntoPro's (now superseded) career framework for software engineers, defining two tracks, five levels, and five shared KPIs each with five steps.
takeaways: Career frameworks (career ladders or competency matrices) help engineers understand how to progress, and a good one answers questions about performance, growth, compensation and hiring.
The framework uses two tracks (Individual Contributor and Manager) with five levels each, where a role is the intersection of a track and a level.
All roles share the same five KPIs (Product, Technology, People, Process, Area of impact), each with five steps; higher steps mean bigger expectations.

Promotions are descriptive, not prescriptive: engineers are promoted after they have demonstrated performance at the next level, and the criteria are conscious, comfortable, continuous, consistent competency.
The page notes that this version is out-of-date and that the latest version is in ProntoPro's handbook, so treat it as a historical example (effective March 2021).
summary.summary: The article from ProntoPro's engineering blog describes the company's renewed Growth framework for software engineers, explaining why it replaced the old one (team growth from 5 to 20+ engineers, move to cross-functional teams, shift from quantitative to qualitative KPIs). It lists the companies used as inspiration and outlines the two career tracks, the five shared KPIs and their step-by-step expectations per role, the four-level evaluation scale, and the promotion philosophy. Detailed descriptions of each KPI step are included at the end. The page itself warns that this version is out-of-date and was effective from March 2021.
